undoRedo.title: Undo buffer
undoRedo.lead: Drag the blocks, add one, delete one, rename one. Every gesture writes actions into a single buffer, and the buffer collapses before it is sent.
undoRedo.connecting: Now pick the second block — the link appears, or goes away.
undoRedo.hint: Drag a block, or tap one to select it. A whole drag is one action — ⌘Z undoes the gesture, not a frame of it.
undoRedo.coverage: Six action types here, forty-odd in the editor. The mechanism does not count them.

canvasFps.title: The frame budget
canvasFps.lead: One scene, one animation, two ways of getting a frame onto the screen. Flip the mode and watch the counter: the difference is not the machine, it is what the code finds to do between frames.
canvasFps.canvas: A field of blocks and links
canvasFps.hint: The modes are measured one at a time: there is a single main thread, and two scenes side by side would fight over it. The first thirty frames after a switch are thrown away as warm-up. Hit pause and compare the “loop” line.
canvasFps.naiveNote: Block positions live in reactive state, and the frame repaints the whole scene through left/top — properties that go through layout. Then a pass over the links reads each block's rectangle and immediately places a link from it: measure, write, measure, write. Every write dirties layout, and every next measurement makes the browser recompute it synchronously, in the middle of the frame.
canvasFps.budgetNote: Same work — every block and every link is repositioned, with no cleverness about updating only what changed. Two things differ: coordinates come from the array instead of being read back off the DOM, so nothing forces a layout mid-pass; and only transform is written, which reaches the compositor without going through layout. While paused, no frame is scheduled at all.
